what: Public replay, written before the run: Itemator's card logic (itemator.ci.facts with rules v6, no team policy, no registry look-up, no model, no Duo credits) run read-only on public merge requests that GitLab Duo's Developer Flow opened from an issue, and on merged merge requests people wrote in the same project. Nothing is posted anywhere.

G.label: GitLab Duo Developer Flow merge requests in GitLab's own codebase
G.select: state merged, merged_at from 2026-09-01T00:00:00Z to before 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z, source_branch starts with 'duo/', and at least one system note by the account 'duo-developer-gitlab-org' on the merge request (a branch name alone is not enough: some people name their own branches duo/)

F.label: GitLab Duo Developer Flow merge requests in the hackathon field (other entrants' public projects)
F.select: any state, created before 2026-10-16T00:00:00Z, source_branch starts with 'duo/', and at least one system note by 'duo-developer-gitlab-ai-hackathon'
F.cap_rule: for the capped figure, take each project's first five by created_at; the uncapped figure is reported as well

H.label: Merged merge requests people wrote in GitLab's own codebase, same month (the comparison)
H.select: state merged, merged_at in the same September window, source_branch does NOT start with 'duo/', author not a bot (username contains 'bot' or starts with 'project_' or 'group_'), no system note by any 'duo-' service account, and a closing link in the description to an issue of the same project that lists this merge request in issues/:iid/closed_by

C.label: Community contributions to GitLab's own codebase (people outside GitLab, the open-source contribution path)
C.select: amendment 2: merged in the same September window, labelled 'Community contribution', source branch not duo/, author not a bot, no system note by any duo- account, and a closing word followed by a same-project issue (as #N or as the issue's URL) whose issues/:iid/closed_by lists this merge request; the first such issue is the one the card reads
C.overlap: a community merge request that closes its issue as #N is also in H; C is reported on its own, never added to H

order: closes_issues (GitLab's own list, as the CI job reads it)
closing words in the description (itemator.ci.closing_refs, as the CI job reads them)
for G and F only, when both are empty: the issue the flow was started from, from a system note by the flow account 'mentioned in issue #N' or else the number in the branch name duo/<kind>/<N>-...
linked_issue.unreadable: an issue the API does not return (404, confidential) is dropped; a merge request with no readable issue is excluded and counted
linked_issue.report_both: every figure is also given for the merge requests the CI job itself would link (the first two sources only)

version_rule.agent: of the merge request's diff versions (merge_requests/:iid/versions, oldest first), the newest one whose commits are all authored by the flow (author_name 'Duo Developer' or an author email containing 'service_account'), with at least one changed file; a merge request with no such version is excluded from the agent figure and counted
version_rule.merged_or_latest: the final diff, whatever the state (field merge requests may be open or closed)

exclusions: a diff GitLab withholds (too_large or collapsed) is scored as a file without a patch and counted

outcome.primary: share of merge requests in G (agent version) whose card would list at least one extra, with a Wilson 95% interval
secondary: the same share for G merged, F agent (capped and uncapped), H merged
extras per flagged merge request, by kind
how many merge requests the CI job would link to an issue by itself
outcome.not_measured_here: whether a listed extra is real: that is the labelling step, with its own rubric, written before it runs

published: For G and H: merge request references, paths and the rules' output (no diff text). For F: counts only, projects replaced by a short hash; the references stay outside the repository. No diff text from any project is committed; diffs are cached under eval/cache/ (gitignored).
limits: One month of one large project for G and H; one hackathon field for F; the flow's agent is one agent; the rules are fixed rules with known false positives (results/precision_audits.json). A flag means the card would ask a person to name something, not that the agent did something wrong: an extra is often a sound change the issue simply did not name. The API gives no file sizes, so the rule for an added file over 1 MB cannot fire, and a diff GitLab withholds counts as a file with no lines; the CI job reads git itself and has both.
smoke_check: Before this file was committed, the scorer ran on our own merge request !94 (outside every population): it gave the one extra the live card gave (.gitlab-ci.yml).

amendment_1.written: 2026-10-16, after the first run and before amendment 1 ran
amendment_1.why: The first run (results/public_replay.json, kept unchanged) could score the agent's own version for only 21 of the 96 linked merge requests in G: for a superseded diff version GitLab's API returns the commits but no diff, so 75 were excluded as having no version with only the flow's commits. A check on three of them showed the repository still holds both commits.
amendment_1.change: When a version's diff is not served, it is rebuilt with repository/compare from that version's base commit to its head commit (straight). Nothing else changes: the same frame, rules, linking, version choice, exclusions and summary. Results go to results/public_replay_a1.json and results/public_replay_a1_raw.json; the first run's files stay as they are and both are reported.

amendment_2.written: 2026-10-16, after amendment 1 ran and before C's frame was built
amendment_2.why: The user asked to test Itemator on GitLab's open-source contribution side. In the cached September list, 267 merged merge requests carry the 'Community contribution' label (92 authors, 250 from forks); counting them looked at labels and closing words only, not at any card.
amendment_2.change: Adds population C (above) with python3 eval/replay_gitlab.py --frame-c, then --amendment 2 --score and --amendment 2 --summarize (results/public_replay_a2.json and _raw). G, F and H are not re-scored. C reads the issue its frame confirmed, because GitLab's closes_issues is empty for a merged merge request (seen in G and in D1's check of 100).
